steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Cook the noodles according to package directions.
Brown the ground beef in a large skillet over medium high heat. Stir in the tomato soup, Worcestershire sauce and garlic, bring to a boil, reduce heat to low and let simmer.

When noodles are done, stir them and the cheese into the simmering sauce until cheese is melted. Stir the sherry into the sauce and stir for 1 minute, then place in a 2 quart casserole dish and sprinkle with the Parmesan cheese to taste.
Bake in preheated oven for 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Beef and Noodle Casserole
raw_recipe.description: Condensed tomato soup makes the sauce for this easy to prepare baked casserole. Cheddar cheese, Worcestershire sauce, and garlic provide additional flavor.
raw_recipe.name: Beef and Noodle Casserole

review.reviewBody: I made this exactly as prepared and it was delicious. The only advice I can give is to be sure and not over-cook the noodles, maybe even just cook them al dente to be sure they don't come out mushy. Excellent combination of flavors! This will be one of our favorites.
Used one can tomato soup and one can of golden mushroom soup. 1 tablespoon of sherry and substituted a 1/2 cup cream cheese for the cheddar. Sooo good. Doesn’t need to bake for 30 minutes
I made it as described except I used small shell pasta instead of the egg noodles. This was quick and easy, We are it all! Next time I will double the recipe so we can have leftovers for lunch.

Pretty Good! - Didn't have sherry used Chianti instead. Kids loved it. I agree with the baking.- No Need. It was actually better fresh out of the pan (when I was tasting). The oven made it dry. Will make again.

I made this two nights ago and it got a big old thumbs up from my family. I actually put the noodles in uncooked and increased the water to 1 cup, then the baking time to 1 hour and it was really good.
Thanks for sharing!!!!

This is an easy and delicious recipe...although I made some changes: I skipped the sherry, substituted jarred pasta sauce for the tomato soup, substituted shredded mozzarella for the cheddar, and added ground black pepper. I've made it with both lean ground beef and lean ground turkey.

We really enjoyed this and it was a snap to put together! I used whole wheat egg noodles instead of regular and sauteed a chopped onion along with the ground beef. My husband LOVED it! It's a great weeknight meal and very satisfying.

Great base, can be 5-star with changes: I replaced one can of soup with a can of tomato sauce, reduced W sauce, cheese and sherry a little, added green pepper, onion and garlic. Baked for 15 minutes, then sprinkled with parm and continued. Like Homemade Hamburger Helper!

5 stars with a few modifications. I used one can on low sodium tomato soup and one 6 oz. can of tomato paste. I also added some Italian seasonings and used whole wheat penne pasta. My 5 year old said "100 stars"! The 2.5 liked it too.

Not a gourmet meal but deserves 5 stars in my book. It it not only tastes good but it's quick and easy. I added a little chopped onion and some italian seasoning while the ground beef was browing. I only had 1 can of tomato soup so I substitued a can of golden mushroom for the second can of soup. I also substitued red wine for the sherry. I baked it in the oven as directed and it didn't come out dry at all. Great recipe, thanks for sharing!
VERY good. I added about a cup each of sauteed celery, onion and green pepper. It just added a bit more interest and alot more flavor.
delicious and super easy, and that means something coming from me because i am an extremely lazy cook. i added in sliced mushrooms to get some veggies into it.

This recipe just was not that good for as much trouble as it was. Boiling noodles, grating cheese, chopping garlic and frying up hamburger for something that was just barely average? Definitely not a weeknight dinner because of multiple steps involved, and certainly not delicious enough to be worthy of a weekend dinner.
I made this on the fly cause I couldn't think of anything to make with ground beef. We all enjoyed it I made it per instructions except no sherry. It still turned out good and the kids loved it
I will add this to my list of "do not make". I think a pasta sauce would be better than soup.
Added a little Italian seasoning, & a can of corn (drained) into the casserole just to add a little sweetness. Overall a really good recipe that my family loved, even the little one yr. old!
I did not care for this recipe.

This recipe is fantastic! My husband and I both loved it. The only thing I changed was because I only had 1 can of tomato soup, so also added a small can of tomato paste and a can of water. Everything else stayed the same and it is really a keeper. ( I love this website.)

This is an awesome meal! I love it! Sometimes I make it with out the meat if I dont have it! Either way I love it! Thanks for sharing the meal, I loved it!

 Your Fan,
 Ivy Liedl
tried it with elbow noodles and no sherry and it turned out great!
